title: Regulatory Plasticity of the Human Genome.
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习模型分析人类基因组增强子调控周转，虽涉及转录因子结合位点，但核心是调控元件进化而非TF-DNA互作机制建模，方法可借鉴但对象和互作深度有限。
abstract: Evolutionary turnover in noncoding regions has driven phenotypic divergence during past speciation events and continues to facilitate environmental adaptation through variants. We used a deep learning model to identify the substrates of regulatory turnover using genome-wide mutations mimicking three evolutionary pathways: recent history (human-chimp substitutions), modern population (human population variation), and mutational susceptibility (random mutations). We observed enhancer turnover in approximately 6% of the whole genome, with more than 80% of the novel activity arising from repurposing of enhancers between cell types. Frequency of turnover in a cell type is remarkably similar across the three pathways, despite only  approximately 19% overlap in the source regions. The majority of turnover loci were found to be localized within 100 kb of a gene, with the highest turnover occurring near neurodevelopmental genes including CNTNAP2, NPAS3, and AUTS2. Flanking enhancers of these genes undergo high turnover irrespective of the mutational model pathway, suggesting a high plasticity in neurocognitive evolution. Based on susceptibility to random mutations, these enhancers were identified as vulnerable by nature and feature a higher abundance of cell type-specific transcription factor binding sites. Our findings suggest that enhancer repurposing within vulnerable loci drives regulatory innovation while keeping the core regulatory networks intact.
abstract_zh: 非编码区域的进化更替在过去物种形成事件中驱动了表型分化，并持续通过变异促进环境适应。我们使用深度学习模型，通过模拟三种进化路径的全基因组突变来识别调控更替的底物：近期历史（人-黑猩猩替换）、现代群体（人类群体变异）和突变易感性（随机突变）。我们观察到全基因组约6%的区域存在增强子更替，其中超过80%的新活性源于增强子在细胞类型间的重新利用。尽管三种路径的源区域重叠仅约19%，但各细胞类型中的更替频率却惊人地相似。大多数更替位点位于基因100 kb范围内，其中最高更替发生在神经发育基因附近，包括CNTNAP2、NPAS3和AUTS2。这些基因的侧翼增强子无论突变模型路径如何均表现出高更替率，提示神经认知进化具有高度可塑性。基于对随机突变的易感性，这些增强子被识别为天然脆弱的，并富含细胞类型特异性转录因子结合位点。我们的发现表明，脆弱位点内的增强子重新利用驱动调控创新，同时保持核心调控网络完整。
